correctness.rationale: For the precisely defined 16-vertex Q4 independence complex, every nonempty face is enumerated by a distinct 16-bit mask (742 faces). A complete 367-pair matching is supplied and independently regenerated by the verifier; it has one critical vertex and seven critical tetrahedra. The certificate supplies a permutation of all 742 faces satisfying every one of the 2816 Hasse-arrow inequalities in the orientation reversing matched incidences, proving acyclicity exhaustively. Forman discrete-Morse theory then gives a one-vertex seven-three-cell CW model; attaching maps to a point are constant, proving a wedge of seven 3-spheres and torsion-free integral H3 of rank 7. Independent exact binary boundary ranks 15,73,135,86,42,14,2 agree; these field ranks are corroboration, not the source of the integral or homotopy claim.

originality.rationale: The precise seven-sphere homotopy type of Ind(Q4) was not implied by inspected published results on open or cylindrical square-grid independence complexes, cross-cycles in periodic square grids, or general suspensions of triangle-free independence complexes. The closest periodic full-text source explicitly does not compute complete homology. Prior finite counts and generic discrete-Morse theory are not presented as novel. Targeted index searches and owned-history statement comparisons found no exact or stronger covering statement. The possibility of differently phrased or unindexed earlier exact computation remains explicitly recognized.

value.rationale: The 16-vertex Q4 is the canonical first degree-four hypercube and simultaneously the minimal C4-by-C4 fully toroidal square grid. The prior periodic-grid cross-cycle problem makes its full integral homology and homotopy type natural, not an arbitrary sliced statistic. An exact seven-S3 wedge and explicit verifiable discrete-Morse certificate provide information strictly beyond known face counts and alternating statistics: simply connectivity, precise torsion-free integral H3 rank and triviality of all other reduced homology. The finite exact datum is a rigorous benchmark for periodic-grid computations. No unproved generalization or unsupported downstream theorem is asserted.
